communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Regarding Mr. Mark Munroe, who formerly served in the Fire/Rescue Department of the Massachusetts Port Authority ("the Authority"). I understand that the Authority employed this individual from about 1993 to about 2013.

1.  Dates of employment. Records sufficient to show his date of hire, his date of separation and any break in service.
2.  Ranks and titles. Records sufficient to show each rank or job title he held in the Fire Rescue Department (for example firefighter, lieutenant, captain or deputy chief), including any acting or temporary rank, and the dates he held each.
3.  Responsibilities and assignments. For each rank or title he held: (a) the job description or position posting in effect at the time; (b) records sufficient to show his assignments, with dates, including station, shift or group, unit, and any command, supervisory or specialty role (for example shift commander or training officer); and (c) any department roster or organizational chart that shows his rank and assignment.
4.  Separation. Records sufficient to show how his employment ended (resignation, retirement, termination or other), and any separation, severance or settlement agreement between him and the Authority.
5.  Discipline. Records of any disciplinary action taken against him, showing for each the date, the action taken (such as a reprimand, suspension or demotion) and the reason. Also, payroll or attendance records showing any period of suspension or administrative leave, with dates.

An extract or report from the Authority's human resources or payroll system, such as a job history report, that shows the information in items 1 and 2 would satisfy those items. 950 CMR 32.07(1)(f).

I am not requesting pay, medical information, home address or other personal contact details, his date of birth, or Social Security number. Please redact those details and release the rest of any record that contains them.

The Authority may consider some of these records, such as disciplinary reports, to be personnel information under exemption (c), M.G.L. c. 4, § 7(26)(c). That exemption does not protect a public employee's name or job classification, or payroll and attendance records showing dates. Pottle v. School Comm. of Braintree, 395 Mass. 861, 862 (1985); Brogan v. School Comm. of Westport, 401 Mass. 306, 308–309 (1987). Nor does it allow a separation or settlement agreement to be withheld as a whole. Globe Newspaper Co. v. Exec. Office of Admin. & Fin., Suffolk Super. Ct. No. 2011-01184-A (June 14, 2013) (the Authority was a party). If the Authority withholds any record or part of one, please identify what is withheld and the specific exemption relied on, and release any segregable portion. M.G.L. c. 66, § 10(a), (b)(iv).

It is expected this should take well under the four hours of staff time that an agency provides without charge. M.G.L. c. 66, § 10(d)(ii). I look forward to your response within 10 business days of receiving this request, as § 10 requires.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Marcus Stewart
